rubric.executionConsistency: No statement contradicts actual compilation, execution or expected/actual values.
rubric.citationValidity: Every cited ID exists in the current request; no AST evidence means not applicable.
rubric.evidenceInterpretation: Claims are supported by code or execution, not merely an existing ID.
rubric.earlyDisclosure: For failing submissions, evidence and hint 1 must not give the corrected token, condition or complete solution. Raw javac diagnostics are allowed as evidence; restating their fix in hint 1 fails. Borderline disclosures are uncertain, not pass.
rubric.falseWarning: On passing submissions, do not invent a defect; optional simplification is not a defect warning.
rubric.resubmissionComparison: For dependent cases, explicitly connect old/current code and test changes; partial-fix must retain the mixed failure. Unknown changes must remain unknown.
rubric.caseRequirements: Also check each case's required and forbidden statements. Keep separate per-axis labels: pass, fail, uncertain, not_applicable.

limits: Same small sum problem; three trials are not population-level reliability. Dependent cases use each version's first response, so their context differs. No independent human grader.
